text_fidelity_a:
Aileho Kids Waterproof Camera Best Pool Toy for Children Birthday Gifts 1080P Kid Digital Underwater Camcorder Sports Action Cam 4 5 6 7 8 9 10 Year Girls 32G SD Card (Dark Purple) [[VIDEOID:e832f455c8dfddb522ae3bbc1ec73698]] Loved the idea of an underwater camera for kids, and this one would have been great if not for the terrible image quality that would only disappoint any except maybe youngest of kids.

When I unpacked the box, I had great expectations. The waterproof shell seemed to be solid and to seal well, and there was a whole lot of extra parts to attach the camera to a bicycle and so on. Camera is very small, but the little screen is bright and it shows the image you're taking clearly. The interface is intuitive and reasonably simple. (I didn't bother to set the date before trying out the camera, but the instructions were clear, and I was able to test it with no problem, it works.)

HOWEVER: I can't believe how bad quality of the images are! They look jagged and pixelated like they're at 480 pixels. Even when I increased the quality in the settings to maximum image resolution, which is supposed to be 20Mb and 7344 pixels (more than what I shoot at for my professional photography biz), the quality stayed the same and the file size only crept up to just below 1 Meg. No idea how they managed to accomplish that. Their image sensor is at about the quality of those blurry, pixelated security cameras that are completely useless for identification. Otherwise, this camera focuses surprisingly well and handles a wide range of light conditions automatically. All the images were in a good range.

The video was marginally better, but still not what you'd expect at 1080 resolution. Camera was recognized by my Windows laptop right away, and I was able to access and copy images with no problem.

It's such a shame that the manufacturer decided to save money on image quality and it's a weird business decision that makes an otherwise fun and well built product useless.

Photos above were taken by the reviewed camera:
- The instruction manual image at highest resolution, and you can see its file size in the second screenshot image. Taken without the waterproof case.
- First Batman toy image at default resolution, without waterproof case
-Second Batman toy image at default resolution, with waterproof case on. Surprisingly, not much difference. Good plastic.
text_fidelity_b: Aileho Kids Waterproof Camera Best Pool Toy for Children Birthday Gifts 1080P Kid Digital Underwater Camcorder Sports Action Cam 4 5 6 7 8 9 10 Year Girls 32G SD Card (Dark Purple)

Only issue is the coil whine, which is a roll of the dice. Worst case scenario it'll whine all the time like the first one I tried, whereas my newest replacement only does it during memory tests - which is acceptable.

But other than that, it's excellent. The Carbon and Strix-E both had issues getting my 7200 kit stable at XMP, and I spent almost a week straight tweaking voltages on the Strix - it would always eventually error out in Karhu after 30-60 minutes or so. The Master however is rock solid, and I was able to OC to 7400cl34 with extreme stability. Its "Low Latency/High Bandwidth" options are excellent, and perform better than the XMP tweaked setting on the ASUS.

It also ran the 13900k the coolest, and seemed easier to get stable. Overall if you are lucky enough to not have one with coil whine, it's definitely the best option in this price range.

text_fidelity_a:
Fit & Fresh Protective Laptop Sleeve with Zippered Storage Pocket, Laptop Bag fits Apple/Microsoft/Acer/Samsung/Google/Lenovo with up to 15.6" Displays, Space Dyed, Gray I have a wonderful hybrid laptop/tablet but the problem is that I needed a case that was slim, but would protect my laptop even while it was being charged. I had a few dings in it from banging on edges of things, so when I saw this, I was hoping it would be perfect. Let's see what happened..

WHAT IS THIS SLEEVE LIKE?
I have backpacks, and big cases to put laptops in, but I just wanted a protective sleeve. That is precisely what this is. It is a fabulous protective sleeve for protecting the laptop. It is lined in very soft velveteen. There is a zipper pocket on the front which has a metal zipper, but is lined with BRIGHT LIME GREEN LINING. I am sorry. I had to capitalize that because I am so excited about it. It is slick so anything put inside will slide in and out easily. It matches the small colored patch on either end of the sleeve.

The outside of the sleeve is like dark denim in color. It is tougher than denim, however. The inside is a light gray. All edges are bound in tough nylon so there are no edges to fray. Workmanship is excellent on this. It is well made.

DOES IT FIT?
My laptop is a 15inch laptop and it fits perfectly. The most exciting part is that I can leave it unzipped and it gives me the room to leave the recharging jack in the laptop so I can recharge it while protecting it. When not recharging, I can zip it shut, put the charger in the pocket and be on my way. I can also zip from both sides leaving the top open if I want and the cord can still come out for recharging. (It has a two way zipper with two zipper heads on each end).

THE BOTTOM LINE
For a protective sleeve that is fresh looking and protective, this is a winner for me. It is soft inside, bright lined outside pocket, and strong workmanship all around. I am very happy with this and highly recommend it.

MY RATING
Five stars for this.
text_fidelity_b: Fit & Fresh Protective Laptop Sleeve with Zippered Storage Pocket, Laptop Bag fits Apple/Microsoft/Acer/Samsung/Google/Lenovo with up to 15.6" Displays, Space Dyed, Gray

text_fidelity_a:
Geeni Sentry Wi-Fi Wireless Smart Floodlight Security Camera, 2-Way Audio, Motion Sensor Alarm, Audio Video Recording, Works with Alexa and Hey Google I have had the opportunity to review a few similar products over the last couple years and this new security light by Sentry has some great features that make it a stand out among other security lights.

I found installation straightforward and simple. For those who have trouble connecting to your WiFi, the most common issue is the strength of the different frequencies your router is broadcasting. The easiest way to resolve this is to go into your router settings via your computer and turn off the 5 GHz band during setup. This is necessary sometimes when initially setting up SmartHome products. While some may find this necessary for this product, I did not using my Orbi router system.

The Geeni App is easy to use and makes setup and customization of how the light operates user friendly.

This unit puts out a huge amount of light - 2100 Lumens to be exact while only using 24 watts of power thanks to it utilizing the LED bulbs.

This is the first security bulb I have reviewed that actually has a built in siren. This could be an outstanding feature if needed. Whether utilized to scare off someone attempting to break in to your home or to cause unwanted pests to run the other way - it will work! This siren is effective because it’s loud.

The speaker can also be used for communication purposes. By utilizing a built in microphone you’ll be able to have conversations with those you are viewing through the camera. The speaker and microphone have a surprisingly high clarity. The only thing I found odd with this aspect of this product is this is not a light you’ll want to place at head height as the light is so bright and the camera is really made to provide a wide angle view. Therefore when you speak through the speaker I found people usually look around and can’t figure out the source of the disembodied voice.

After using this product for the last 6 weeks I have found that it performs excellently. By installing a 128GB micro SD card within it, saving videos is easy and I’ve had plenty of time to review the footage. I love that it holds the recording locally so there is no cloud subscription fee required.

This is an excellent security light that will not only light the night when motion is detected, but will record it, alert you, scare the intruder with a siren or allow you to speak to them (or apologize for just scaring them with the siren).

This is an outstanding product that I definitely recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Geeni Sentry Wi-Fi Wireless Smart Floodlight Security Camera, 2-Way Audio, Motion Sensor Alarm, Audio Video Recording, Works with Alexa and Hey Google

text_fidelity_a:
Soundcore Wakey Bluetooth Speaker Powered by Anker with Alarm Clock, Stereo Sound, FM Radio, White Noise, QI Wireless Charger with 7.5W Charging for iPhone and 10W for Samsung I ordered the 'Soundcore Wakey Bluetooth Speaker Powered by Anker with Alarm Clock, Stereo Sound, FM Radio, White Noise, QI Wireless Charger with 7.5W Charging for iPhone and 10W for Samsung' for review and would like to share some of my thoughts after a few weeks.

First off, this thing is actually pretty amazing. The build quality is nice and aesthetically it looks clean. The sound quality is nice but not phenomenal. However for how small it is, it does produce decent sound and for a bedside alarm clock it does quite well. The wireless charging works great for my Galaxy Note 8 (and does in fact Fast-Charge) however there have been a couple nights to where my phone was not charged the next morning. The fast charger also works with my wireless earbuds which I attached an image showing the charge light on the Wakey, and the wireless earbuds case indicating charging. However for the wireless earbud charging, it does take some precise positioning to get them to charge. I noticed in other review that others weren't happy with the bright display light with no way to adjust it any dimmer than the lowest setting, however they must have updated that with a firmware update (which was super easy to do) as I had no issues with the display being too bright at night. I use the auto adjust setting which seems to work quite well as far as I can tell. Also I love the sleep mode sounds that you can adjust several (or just one) sound volumes to create your own personalized preference. I do wish that there were more sound options but the ones they provide are acceptable. I also wish that you could download and install more alarm sounds. Bluetooth connectivity is super quick and have never once had an issue with pairing it up to my phone. Really the ONLY issue I have with the Wakey is that to get the sleep mode sounds going, you need to connect with the app, and via Bluetooth connect to the device. No big deal right? Well my concern is that you will need to keep it connected for this feature to work. This means you will be connected to the Wakey ALL night and this kind of bugs me. It's just kind of creepy that the Wakey is connected to your phone all night while you sleep. I wish there was a way to just play your favorite white noise sleep sound by pressing a button on the Wakey device without having to always connect and stay connected to the app and your phone. The other gripe is that the plug design is huge and makes it so that I have had to move my nightstand further way from the wall to use it. Other than those two gripes, and the only reason for docking one star, the Soundcore Wakey is a very good product and a really great value.
*On a side note - I just tested the Wakey while watching some Youtube videos and the latency is not so good. There is quite a bit of delay and the voices do not sync up at all so I wouldn't recommend using the Wakey for listening to videos.
text_fidelity_b: Soundcore Wakey Bluetooth Speaker Powered by Anker with Alarm Clock, Stereo Sound, FM Radio, White Noise, QI Wireless Charger with 7.5W Charging for iPhone and 10W for Samsung

text_fidelity_a: StarTech.com 2 Port USB DVI KVM Switch with DDM Fast Switching Technology and Cables - Dual Port DVI USB KVM Switch - DDM KVM Switch (SV231DVIUDDM) If you remember the old game unit switches that allowed you to use multiple devices on one television set, this is like that, only for two computers sharing one monitor, keyboard, mouse, and other peripherals. The simple switch box connects to your monitor ("console") via the kind of cord with plugs on both ends you currently use to connect your monitor to your computer. (You will need an extra cord like this for the the purpose--not included. If you don't have a spare lying around, you should order one with the unit.) You will need the cords you are currently using for each of the two computers to connect them to the box. There are four USB sockets in the "console" section of the box. You plug your keyboard, mouse, and anything else you want to share between the two computers into those. (By the way, KVM stands for Keyboard, Video,Mouse.) The unit is powered, and offers multiple plug styles for international use. There is a place to plug in speakers and a mike for each computer. This switch has made it possible for me to streamline my office space considerably. Previously, I had two monitors, two keyboards, and two mice. It was very awkward. I kept my old computer because it has Adobe CS4, which is fine for my needs and saves me the $50 a month the Creative Cloud would cost. I have not used it much, though. Firing up the old machine was just too much trouble. This new arrangement allows me to flip a switch and access programs I have not been able to use in a long time.
text_fidelity_b: StarTech.com 2 Port USB DVI KVM Switch with DDM Fast Switching Technology and Cables - Dual Port DVI USB KVM Switch - DDM KVM Switch (SV231DVIUDDM)

Digital Photo Frame 15-inch WiFi Digital Picture Frame - FULLJA Smart Digital Photo Frames 32GB Storage, Easy to Setup and Share Photos and Videos via App or Email, Gifts for Family The Fullja 10 inch WiFi Digital Picture Frame replaces >5-year-old LCD frame. Wow. Excellent upgrade in both hardware and software.

The total frame size is 10" x 7" in practical terms. The IPS (in-plane switching) touch-screen LCD at 1280x800 resolution (189 PPI) is HD, one LCD grade less than FHD. I can't discriminate between HD and FHD resolution from a picture frame's typical viewing distance. The LCD viewing angle is excellent, consistent with the IPS fabrication. This is important, perhaps THE most important criteria for an LCD picture frame. The LCD's backlighting is motion-activated and quite good. Backlighting consumes most of the battery current. Motion detection will extend battery life.

Clock, calendar, and weather update options expand the utility beyond a picture frame. Image connectivity and control include the range from TF portable memory to WiFi. Very cool.

Better than expected. Excellent value for money. One wonders how it can be made at the price.

text_fidelity_a:
Jabra VOX Corded Stereo Headphones I confess, I'm not one for listening to things on earphones. I'm not attached to my iPod (I don't even have one). I don't listen to music on the bus or during lunch or anything like that. I have music on my smartphone, but I usually either plug it into the radio in my car via a cassette adapter and listen to it over the car speakers, or plug it into a speaker we got as a Christmas gift that is for use on music players/smartphones. So I all I had was a coupla dollar set of earphones from Micro Center when I absolutely had to use earphones. They were cheap and comfortable. Really, how much better can a high-priced couple of wires and earpieces be?

Mea culpa. I just did a head-for-head comparison of my cheap little blue earphones against these Jabra units. Wow. With my old earphones I could hear the fan and the television running in the background, and the sound was a bit smothered. When I changed to the Jabra VOX earphones I was awed. They were even more comfortable. The sound from the fan was completely inaudible and I could just, just tell that the television was on behind me, so I'm not saying they're noise canceling, but they do HELP reduce noise. The sound was excellent! The "smothered" sound was non-existent and the bass was especially good (I was listening to a podcast and the host has a nice deep voice). When I switched to music, the sound was much richer and I could hear a wider range of sound, and, again, the bass was excellent.

Plus the earphones come with a free app you can download that organizes your music. You can set playlists, view album covers, and it even has an equalizer.

If good sound is your goal while listening to your music device/smartphone, this is an excellent choice. My old blue earphones are going into the emergency bin as of now!
text_fidelity_b: Jabra VOX Corded Stereo Headphones

text_fidelity_a:
Samsung T3 Portable SSD - 2TB - USB 3.1 External SSD (MU-PT2T0B/AM) I like tech. I've had a computer since the commodore Vic-20 came out. That being said I'm not into competing with or against other computers and computer users. I don't run testing or speed diagnostics on my hardware. If it works and feels or seems to be working as advertised and expected I'm completely happy. I just don't care to sit here are see how many micro-seconds faster my new drive is than my older ones.
All that being said I use external drives exclusively for maintaining backups of my personal files, photos, documents, music, eBooks, Etc. Everything else I can simply reinstall in a couple hours. I don't have that many things installed. My computing needs are simple. But I have lost files due to a drive crash so I meticulously make weekly backups of my important files. Currently I've been using two USB 3.0 Seagate Backup Plus drives to make my backups every Monday.
This new Samsung solid state drive is remarkably faster at copying files to than my mechanical drives and easily a quarter the size and weight of the Seagate drives. I had a couple hiccups when I first formatted the drive to NTFS (I had no need of proprietary encryption) and started copying my files over to the drive but after one or two false starts I got tens of thousands of files copied over with no more problems and have for several weeks just copied new files to the existing collections in their directories and once again this SSD drive flies through the process much faster than the Seagate drives. Now I have three complete backups of my files and feel that much safer and secure with three copies of my files and I love that there's no moving parts. The cable's long enough, about eighteen inches, to work fine with my laptop though someone with a desktop may want to invest in a longer cable.
I'm knocking one star off for a device this expensive not coming with even a cheap hard shell case or even a rubber plug to protect the USB port from dust. It's the one point of possible entry of foreign matter into the drive and causing damage or failure. For the price they're currently charging it wouldn't have been any real hardship to include a case or plug to protect this device.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung T3 Portable SSD - 2TB - USB 3.1 External SSD (MU-PT2T0B/AM)

TomTom Via 1525SE 5 Inch GPS Navigation Device with Free Traffic, Free Maps of the US, Advanced Lane Guidance and Spoken Turn-By-Turn Directions This GPS is a real upgrade for me, but I still love my old one which is TomTom One. Too bad it's no longer supported by TomTom or I probably would not have chosen the TomTom Via 1525 to try out for review. The very first thing I noticed about it was that the screen was twice as large as on my One - a very coveted perk to me. I choose to still use separate GPS devices instead of my phone since my phone uses up data and the GPS doesn't, saving me $$.

I have only used the Via 1525 a couple of times and it worked perfectly. I had to make a new account to TomTom to update it and overall it took about an hour and a half. I had a couple of problems with the update and had to restart but it finally worked. It comes with a USB for charging from a computer and another to use in the auxiliary power port in the car, and a mounting disk to adhere to a good spot in the car. It's not as intuitive as I would like, but it's not hard to figure out and it took us straight to our destination both times. I purposely passed some streets it was telling to me turn on to just to see how fast it would recalculate a route and it recalculated quickly. It has a lot of options that are indicated on the product page, most of which I will probably not use.

It's too early yet to give it 5 stars, but definitely 4 for now. It's a GPS, it found satellites quickly, got me a route planned out and was easy to follow. What more do I want from it? I like it a lot. It's supposed to have lifetime traffic and lifetime maps.......or until TomTom stops supporting it too.
text_fidelity_b: TomTom Via 1525SE 5 Inch GPS Navigation Device with Free Traffic, Free Maps of the US, Advanced Lane Guidance and Spoken Turn-By-Turn Directions

I'm glad I chose this one. It is working well. The instructions are not great, so you have to figure out how to get it to work. Lesson #1: save to a local hard drive. I store my video files on a large external (USB) drive, and when I had Elgato save directly to the external drive, I got errors and it wouldn't work. I thought the product was a dud. Then I switched to ripping to the local drive, and it works every time. Sometimes the audio and video are not in sync at first try, but has always worked the second try. It is also sensitive to your sound card drivers: if you try to use other audio applications (e.g. iTunes, Amazon Music, DAWs) while recording, the recording will be corrupted. So you either have to leave your computer alone while recording, or only use apps that don't use audio. The instructions don't tell you how to trim the video, but you can do that with the sliders; had to figure that one out on my own. Because of these little annoyances, I only gave it 4 stars.

text_fidelity_a: Loigys Wireless Keyboard, 2.4G Full-Sized Ergonomic Wireless Computer Keyboard with Wrist Rest for Windows, Mac OS Laptop/PC/Desktop/Notebook (Black) This is advertised as an ergonomic keyboard.  To me, ergonomic is a keyboard that is split into two slanted halves, like the Microsoft Natural Keyboard.  This is a flat keyboard.  In spite of that, the keys have a good feel and response.  I only have wired keyboards, so I got this so that I could have a wireless if I wanted to use one sometimes, as you are then not confined with a cord.  Requires 1 AA battery to operate (not included).  At first, I thought they forgot to include the wireless transmitter, but it comes hidden in the battery compartment.  This is okay, but there is no place to store it once the battery is installed.  Of course, if you are going to store the keyboard and not use it all the time, you wouldn't typically want to leave the battery in anyway.  If you want wireless, probably better to get a wireless mouse and keyboard together, as they would probably run off one transmitter, whereas with this keyboard if I want to add a wireless mouse later, it will involve using a second transmitter which would use another USB port.  The keyboard is going to be of limited use to me, as I currently use a KVM-switch that allows me to control up to 4 computers with one monitor, one mouse and one keyboard.  I would have to upgrade to a KVM switch that takes USB to use the keyboard on more than one computer.  This is truly plug and play and I had it operating in no time at all.  Seems like it is quality made and should last a while.  Made in China of course.
text_fidelity_b: Loigys Wireless Keyboard, 2.4G Full-Sized Ergonomic Wireless Computer Keyboard with Wrist Rest for Windows, Mac OS Laptop/PC/Desktop/Notebook (Black)

I've purchased three of these keyboard/mouse sets since January 2018 and I think it's one of the best pieces of equipment that I've added to my computer set up. I run 3 to 4 laptops every day, each one accomplishes a different task for me. It was getting to be a real pain having to stand up and stretch across the desk to enter a password or move the mouse and these solved that problem for me. It did take some getting used to at first since each set looks exactly alike but I have that worked out with their placements. LOL!

The set in the photo is the first set that I purchased on January 29, 2018. This set is used for HOURS darn near every day. I write online content so my keyboards always take a beating. This one has held up BEAUTIFULLY and, as a bonus, I've only had to replace the battery in the mouse once. My guess is that somehow I got super charged batteries in the keyboard because it is still going on the originals. The other two sets are still running off of 100% original batteries.

There isn't one thing that I can complain about with this set. I like that there are little flip out legs on the bottom/back part of the keyboard that allow it to lean up in the back. It makes it much easier to use. I like that there can be some distance between the keyboard/mouse and the computer when being used and I LOVE that there are no wires to deal with.

All in all it's a great set that is worth the money. I have three of these sets and each one is fantastic.

A tiny speaker the size of a soda can that creates a wonderful sound environment. I have it hooked to my Echo dot and the sound clarity is really good! And the bass coming out of the top is pretty precise. It's not the thundering bass but the correct one (to my ears). Takes up really a very small space.

Set up was very easy. Pressed a button to pair it with Echo using Bluetooth. My phone and Echo both picked it up really quick. Can't really tell if it's going to work in long distance but I have no reason to doubt what the manufacturer is claiming.

The only issue I had was figuring out how to use the volume buttons. I assume it's a quick press to lower or increase the volume but it's actually a long press. And then I am not sure how long to hold down the button to increase and decrease since there's no visual cue. But once I found the right volume it's OK. I can control the actual volume from the source as well.

Koss 155524 UR40 Collapsible Over-Ear Headphones ...and after 13 years of heavy use, I was curious... here's my old headphones!

I went looking, because I like them so much all this time!

A couple things.

The mesh head thing- it only stayed on a couple years. They headphones worked better without it anyhow I think. Smoother on my hair. Which has a fine texture, and is a bit frizzy- lots of fine short pieces. Sometimes the foldable joints catch in them. This happens on earrings, necklaces, other headphones and other things as well. No more on this product really. Function of having fine curly hair.

Sound has always been fantastic. I love the sound and am sad when I send a ton of cash on headphones that don't come close.

They are not a snug fit, but, are soft enough and comfy enough to wear to bed. Because of the tender fabric, it's started to deteriorate on the smooth fake leathery bits. So so soft all this time though. Really to last 13 years, NO COMPLAINTS!!!.

Not snug enough to work out in. Snug enough to casually hike or walk in. They won't just fall right off or anything.

Lightweight. Easy to make a pouch or toss them into a ziplock freezer quart bag to travel and keep them in your pack or bag more tidily.

I would agree with most reviews. I tend to consider the cables 'supple' instead of 'flimsy'-- and this is an important difference! Supple cables don't just out at awkward angles and get caught on as much stuff. You can keep your music device in your pocket and the cable stays nicely under your coat or shirt and bends where you need it to stay and likes being there rather than tugging intself back in to the shape it wants to be in like a stiffer cable.

These are one of the few products I would give 10 stars to if I could.

And I still would after 13 years!!!!!!

Oh,

Actually they still work fine too. Really. I just noticed they are really a little fiddly nowadays because I used them so much, and was wondering if they still made them.

It's a bit disturbing that amazon remembered I bought them so long ago, though. I'm starting to hope Amazon never holds a grudge against me, cause they never forget!!
text_fidelity_b: Koss 155524 UR40 Collapsible Over-Ear Headphones

text_fidelity_a:
Samsung Galaxy Tab 2 (10.1-Inch, Wi-Fi) 2012 Model I thought long and hard about a tablet, knowing that for me it would basically be a toy. Plus I already had a Nook Color. When the iPad2 reduced in price, I thought about getting one of those, but decided against it for the following reasons: (1) no Flash--and yes, I know HTML5 is going to make that obsolete, but in the meantime many websites have a lot of money invested in Flash animation and even restaurants use the silly format to show you their menus (geez, just give us a LIST already--I don't need pretty pictures to find out if you serve something I can eat) and (2) I'm already invested in the Android market and would have to buy many iPad apps that I already have free from Android.

I have not even used it for a week yet, but this a preliminary review with some information I saw requested in other reviews (not necessarily here at Amazon).

UPS delivered this a little before 6:30 p.m. I immediately plugged it into the charger and left it alone. It was charged by 10 p.m. (it might have been earlier, but the unit was away from me and I heard no bleep or flash that might have have indicated the charge was finished). So it does not take six or eight or ten hours to charge as I have seen claimed on other sites. By midnight I was attached to wireless, had gotten into all my accounts and Android apps and was happily surfing and rearranging my home screen.

I used this over the weekend at a science fiction convention. I did not use it constantly, but turned the screen on and off all day for about a 12-hour period, reading Facebook and blogs, checking the news and weather, looking at the convention schedule online, playing short You Tube videos, etc. Nothing excessive, but sometimes did have it on for a half hour to 45-minutes at the time. I also do not have a lot of widgets going, like the Accu-Weather and news widgets that come pre-loaded on the home screen. (They delete easily.) In that 12-hour period it never got below 78% on the battery. It's very quick and fast and responds to a Targus stylus (rubber tipped) wonderfully, much better than my Nook color. The resolution of the screen is impressive. Maybe it's not the new iPad's "retinal display," but it's very, very sharp and bright, even though I keep my brightness turned down to save power. I downloaded the Nook app and the magazines I subscribe to look gorgeous and are simple to read; if not, a tap of the screen makes the text bigger. The unit also comes with Zinio preloaded, an app I plan to use to subscribe to non-US magazines. Kindle books look nice as well, but to me this is too large for marathon reading sessions. I prefer my Nook Color for that. Like my Android phone and my Nook Color, it connects to wireless like a dream, which is more than I can say for my laptop.

Things that might lead you to choose another tablet: (1) The camera is nothing special. It takes good close ups, but further away was problematic. However, I was in a low-light situation each time. Taking photos outside may be totally different. Why Samsung chose to remove the flash I have no idea. Silly, really. But who buys a tablet to take pictures with? (2) With a stylus I can tap to enlarge an image (like Google Maps), but not make it smaller and there is no plus or minus sign on the screen as on my Android phone. (3) Blogger doesn't work in the browser; you have to download the Blogger app, but that works well. iExit doesn't work on it, either. Rats. (4) As at least one other person mentioned, the screen cap button is right in a place where you can hit it easily. I thought of a good use for it this weekend (took a screen cap of the online schedule for the convention I was at, made a short-cut of it to the screen, then pulled up the screen cap for reference rather than going to the web page all the time). Very convenient! (5) Hate the pre-loaded websites in the browser, but I have seen this on other tablets. Apparently we the public are stupid (or lazy) and can't find our own favorite websites and bookmark them. [eyes roll], and (6) my Bluetooth keyboard won't work with it right now because there is as yet no driver for Android 4.0 (Ice Cream Sandwich).

I hope to check back with further comments.

[A few weeks later after I bought this, my husband found an Asus Transformer (TF300) at a good price. It appears to be just as good as this Samsung and the camera is better. It has a zoom and does take a better photo. So if you were looking for a tablet with a better camera the Asus Transformer may be for you. Note: It doesn't have a flash either.]

[Update July 31, 2012 to answer "How long does the battery last"?: I was sick and tired of not seeing any Olympic equestrian coverage except for a couple of hours in the wee hours of the morning, so downloaded the "Live Extra" Olympics app from the Android Market. This carries live streaming of events as well as archived events. This morning I watched about two hours of live streaming of the jumping finals. When that ended I watched six hours of cross-country eventing replay. Then about an hour and forty minutes of the replay of the jumping. I had my brightness at about 35%. This got me down to 10% of the battery from a full charge. Quite satisfactory.]
text_fidelity_b: Samsung Galaxy Tab 2 (10.1-Inch, Wi-Fi) 2012 Model

text_fidelity_a:
Fujifilm Finepix F70EXR 10MP Super CCD Digital Camera with 10x Optical Dual Image Stabilized Zoom and 2.7 inch LCD This is a high quality camera, but you must take time to read through the owner's manual to understand how to get the best pictures. You can just grab it and point and shoot using it while in the "automode" setting, but the resulting pictures may leave you a little disappointed depending upon the photographic conditions. To get the highest quality photos you must become familiar with how this little beauty works. Unfortunately, you might have to print out and tote the manual with you when you find yourself in situations where your pictures aren't what you'd like, or you can't figure out how to do certain things like know what's behind the flashing icon error message, or how to simulate different types of film, or can you choose between clarity, reduced noise and dynamic range? This is not really a simple "point and shoot" camera and all images will turn out great. You will have to study it, practice with it, and most of all have patience and you will be pleasantly rewarded for your efforts. Though the indicators vary with camera settings, there are 23 different indicators just for shooting mode, and 12 for playback mode, not to mention the date/time stamp, battery level, and indicator. It can get confusing.

Although a basic manual booklet is included with the camera, a much more detailed manual must be uploaded from the enclosed CD and then all 125 pages can be printed out or read from your computer monitor. The manual covers all the material in the booklet almost page for page but includes much more information about features the booklet leaves out and the booklet will refer you to specific pages in the manual for more information. Also, in the manual are about 50 FAQ's that are very useful. I am a manual reader, (having written many technical SOP's) and appreciate having well-written and well thought out manuals that are understandable and succinct. Though I would have preferred a manual that I don't have to upload to my computer, it is well-written and many useful pictures are included.

This camera is loaded with many different options/features but accessing and understanding many of them will require reading the manual. For people who don't want to be bothered with all the bells and whistles this camera may be more than they need. I can see very serious photographers using this camera. Reading through the manual I have compiled a list of some of the various modes, options and features available:

Digital Zoom
Movie Mode
Silent Mode
Variable ISO settings
Image size selection
Aspect Ratio selection
Intelligent Face detection
Scene Position
Shooting Modes
EXR Mode
Film simulation
Dynamic Range
White Balance
Continuous Photography
Photometry - multi, spot, average

Playback Options:
Erase
Slide Show
Red-eye Removal
Image Rotation
Protection from accidental deletion
Crop
Resize
Voice Memo
Print Order
Time Difference
Format

Pages 37, 67-68, 86-87, 97-103, and 104-107 would be good to print out and keep with your camera as they contain tables of various camera functions and a trouble shooting chart.

I have taken many pictures and movies inside and out, light and dark, with this camera set on various settings. And though I have practiced with it now for several weeks, I still need to often refer to the manual when I choose to vary from automode. Some things I have found especially desirable are:

Silent Mode - I attend classical music concerts where flash photography is prohibited. This mode will silence all beeps and flashes.

Large viewing screen on the back of the camera. It is exactly 5.5cm x 4.0 cm.

Digital Zoom - extremely good. I attended a local minor-league baseball game and sat far away on the grass well beyond the playing field. I was able to fully zoom and still get good, clear, close-up shots of the players with no blurring.

Movie Mode - Completely surpasses any other I've experienced so far. Images are clear, colorful and the sound quality is excellent. Camera noise was heard and recorded while using the "zoom" function in Movie Mode though it was not very loud.

Multi-frame play back function is very useful to quickly scan for a particular picture.

Fine Pix Viewer Program was very easy to install on my computer. I use Windows XP.

Very good photography in low-light conditions.

Also some things I did not find particularly desirable but are not major flaws:

I cannot directly burn a CD using the Fine Pix Viewer Program which comes with this camera. I have to use another camera program, import the pictures into it and then burn a CD.

Very easy to accidentally turn it on or off and easy to get misfires.

The zoom lever is too sensitive. I have learned with practice to barely move it very slowly.

The camera does not give helpful suggestions on how to get a better picture as does my HP R717.

Not HD capable.

The higher the ISO the grainier the picture though a higher ISO is desirable when shooting in dim/low light levels. I have set the ISO level to 200 and that seems to produce the best pictures so far.

Almost too many options, modes and functions to choose from. Though you can immediately begin to take pictures using Automode, it will take time to fully understand the many other aspects and features this camera has.

In Summary:

I can find no major complaint concerning this camera. It takes excellent clear and colorful photos even in situations where I least expect it - indoors with no flash. Any poor quality pictures I have taken are not the fault of the camera but due to the photographer's ignorance of how to use/understand properly the many features of the camera. The basic mechanics of such things as battery and memory card installation are very easy. Battery charging is a very simple process and battery life seems long. The manual is detailed and covers more than I would probably care to know. This is almost more camera than I need, though I will continue to use it and will update this review as necessary.

UPDATE 2.9.15 - Been using this camera all these years and now it's beginning to show it's age and giving me some problems. The viewing screen on the back has a vertical big black bar but it doesn't appear on the actual pictures. And the lens cover doesn't always completely open when the camera is turned on. I still use it but it might be time to think about a replacement. It's been good though so I really don't have any complaints.
text_fidelity_b: Fujifilm Finepix F70EXR 10MP Super CCD Digital Camera with 10x Optical Dual Image Stabilized Zoom and 2.7 inch LCD

NETGEAR Orbi Pro WiFi 6 Tri-Band Mesh System (SXK50), Router with 1 Satellite Extender for Business or Home, VLAN, QoS, Coverage up to 5,000 sq. ft, 75 Devices, AX5400 802.11 AX (up to 5.4Gbps) The rise of home automation devices means that many of us have a lot more devices that connect to our wifi networks. While most of those devices use the 2.4Ghz frequency while devices like phones, tablets, and firetv use 5Ghz to stay out of each other's way, it still means that there are so many more devices to manage in a network and all of them are attempting to talk on the network. Not to mention interference from neighbors and their many devices.

This drives the need for beefy routers with faster CPUs to manage all of the chatter and radios that allow many more simultaneously connected devices.

The NETGEAR Orbi Pro WiFi 6 Tri-band Mesh System (SXK80) attempts to address these needs. Sporting the latest wireless Wifi 6 technology, most of the basic features that a router needs (QoS, DDNS, VPN), and 60+ device support, the SKX80 holds a lot of promise.

Unlike one of the upvoted reviews, I don't have a different AX system to compare this to so for me, this mesh router performs admirably. It is fast and has good coverage. In my time so far, I haven't had any dropped connections. Videos stream well and web browsing works fine. I don't normally do voice or video calls while walking around the house, but watching videos while walking seem to work well. My device will jump from router to satellite correctly and there is no disruption to the video playback.
text_fidelity_b: NETGEAR Orbi Pro WiFi 6 Tri-Band Mesh System (SXK50), Router with 1 Satellite Extender for Business or Home, VLAN, QoS, Coverage up to 5,000 sq. ft, 75 Devices, AX5400 802.11 AX (up to 5.4Gbps)

Heysliy Product Photography Light Box 16x16 Inch,Adjustable Bright Photo Box with Lights,Portable Photo Studio Light Box Photoboxes are simple things; It is usually just 5-sided box with some sort of backdrop and a strip of LED. The Heysliy Light Box Photography lightbox is just that and nothing more. Designed to be portable, the box can be folded flat and comes with a carrying bag that nicely stores everything in the kit.

Unfortunately, it's the execution of the thing that is to be desired. The box is cut from a sheet of translucent plastic then folded to form a box. The flaps are joined by a barely-tight-enough screw cap that can be easily lost because it is not actually part of the box. The plastic itself is stuff, but has an elastic memory, which means that it wants to fold back to its storage position, weakening the sides of the box unless the flaps are folded outward first. Overall, the structure is quite flimsy and can be tricky to set up.

The Heysliy lightbox comes with four backdrops made of that paper-like material that is used by some reuseable grocery bags. The colors are black, white, green, and red. The backdrop is hung by a hole cut into the material and a tab that's cut into the plastic box. Any hard tug will rip that backdrop so be careful.

So the conclusion is that the box is annoying to set up and with the LED's mounted on the inside of the box, reflections will be a big issue with this box as can be seen in my pictures (nintendo switch pictured for size reference).
text_fidelity_b: Heysliy Product Photography Light Box 16x16 Inch,Adjustable Bright Photo Box with Lights,Portable Photo Studio Light Box

SOSUN Video Camera Camcorder HD 1080P 24.0MP 3.0 Inch LCD 270 Degrees Rotatable Screen 16X Digital Zoom Camera Recorder and 2 Batteries(301S-Plus), 301AM I haven't bothered with a video camera in many years - using an excellent cell phone camera is just so much easier and convienent. That is still the case when I decide between using this camera vs my LG V40 phone for quick video of the dogs and horses. However, I did take the video camera with me to Big Bend National Park last week and tried it out there.

There are two rechargeable batteries and they offer far more use time than I expected. Swapping them out is pretty simple once you figure out where they go. The instructions are skimpy, but things are reasonably logical. The little carrying case is padded and the entire camera and case fits perfectly in a side pocket of a small hiking pack.

Actual use is straightforward. The camera fits in your palm and the record, photo and zoom buttons are designed to be pressed with just a thumb. I do like the view screen - it rotates and lets you really see what you're filming. For wide, expansive vistas like West Texas offers, this camera is fine and captures the vast distance of the landscape. However, close up details are fuzzy - I sincerely doubt this is true 1080p quality simply because the video shot from my phone is sharper and prettier. text_fidelity_a:
Logitech for Creators Blue Yeti X Professional USB Condenser Microphone for PC, Mac,Gaming,Recording, Streaming, Podcasting on PC, Desktop Mic High-Res Metering, LED Lighting,Blue VO!CE Effects-Black This is a fancier version of the popular Blue Yeti amateur-quality USB microphone with a much higher price tag ($170 vs $110). For the extra money, you get 4 condensers (instead of 3) to give you higher-resolution 24-bit audio (instead of 16-bit) plus a bunch of fancier control and display options. The new microphone has the same directional recording patterns to isolate the recording to your intended audio sources. Is the new microphone worth the extra money? If you really need 24-bit audio, then definitely yes. If not, the new display and control features are more convenient than a huge jump in functionality. The Blue Yeti is still a great microphone for amateur USB recording (podcasts, musical performances, etc). The new version is a step forward, but not worth the price for everyone.

My biggest complaint is that the new microphone uses the same ancient mini-USB interface as the old one. Modern ultralight laptops are moving to the USB-C standard and mini-USB is 2 generations old. You could use a USB-C hub to give you a mini-USB interface, but I wish all modern devices came with USB-C ports since this has been the standard for the last few years.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech for Creators Blue Yeti X Professional USB Condenser Microphone for PC, Mac,Gaming,Recording, Streaming, Podcasting on PC, Desktop Mic High-Res Metering, LED Lighting,Blue VO!CE Effects-Black

text_fidelity_a:
Bestlight 48 LED Macro Ring Light With 6 Adaptors Rings for Canon Digital EOS Rebel SL1 (100D),T5i(700D),T4i(650D),T3(1100D),T3i(600D),60D,60Da,50D,Nikon D5300,D5000,D3000,D3200,D5100 DSLR Cameras 48 LED unit - (since several items are listed under one product ID)
Positives:
- It is what it looks like, does what it claims to do, and basically works
- cheap
- comes with an AC adapter!! Wow. You can pay a lot for a light that doesn't

Negatives: I'm using this for Macro work (I'm new to macro) so that's the perspective I'm coming from
- Not Bright Enough! It's just not all that bright. Not enough to light a subject by itself for macro purposes. I doubt it's adequate for more than a highlight for portraiture. This is why 2 stars. If a light doesn't light - it's not a light.

Really that's it. This is not a knock to the light (and not why I gave it a low rating), but if you are planning on using it for macro, buy a flash instead. A flash will not only have higher output, but will help freeze the camera shake (a big macro problem). Also, I thought the full time light would be better for live insects (you can see what you're doing!), but it's the opposite. You need the flash to freeze action. Not a criticism (this light does not advertise itself as a flash), but something to know.

UPDATE: I used it a couple more times. I am finding it more useful than initially when very close in. I would still strongly recommend a flash for this unless you have a compelling reason for continuous illumination (e.g you're waiting for a bug to crawl into frame and it's too dark to see otherwise. Though the lights would probably scare the bug). If you have a pretty solid tripod setup, this can work for longer exposure macro. Not great though. Upped to 3 stars.
text_fidelity_b: Bestlight 48 LED Macro Ring Light With 6 Adaptors Rings for Canon Digital EOS Rebel SL1 (100D),T5i(700D),T4i(650D),T3(1100D),T3i(600D),60D,60Da,50D,Nikon D5300,D5000,D3000,D3200,D5100 DSLR Cameras

text_fidelity_a: Canon PowerShot SX50 HS 12MP Digital Camera with 2.8-Inch LCD (Black) - International Version (No Warranty) I  loved this little camera. Great features and photos. Sent it to Canon for repair. Got an email saying they didn't work on that part, I'd get a new or refurbished. I called to say i did not want a refurbished camera given that i'd already had problems with two of this model.  Too bad they said, you're getting refurbished.  I asked to talk to customer relations. Got a lady who told me it was in the warranty they could give me refurbished and furthermore they had no new ones to give--this is the CAnon facility mind you.  I called back to try to talk to another rep--was told they couldln't transfer me. Then, when i said i was recording it, and told him i had been transferred last time, suddenly he now could transfer me. Back to initial rep who refused to let me talk to anyone else and refused to budge on sending a new camera, even though it was an option in the email. I wrote letters and emails to management. Got a response, said they'd send me a new camera after i said i had the whole thing on recording and was thinking of posting to youtube. but they wouldn't pay for me to ship the old one back.  Anyway this story goes on and on, including me mailing the camera back and being told it actually WAS a new one and they were shipping the same camera back to me.  Was a nightmare. I don't know if any of the other companies are better, but i've been a solid Canon customer for 20 years--as i told them--and I won't be anymore.  They need to take lessons from Amazon on customer service.  Hope this camera lasts awhile as I know now it won't get serviced properly without it being more trouble than it's worth.

Leather Laptop Messenger Bag for Men - Handmade Laptop Briefcase Satchel by Leather Centric This LEATHER LAPTOP MESSENGER BAG FOR MEN (by Leather Centric) is made of real leather--animal hide, NOT the man-made “pleather” stuff that’s often marketed on Amazon as “real leather” or “genuine leather”. That’s a big plus, but the bag itself has a lot of minuses.

First, the bag’s styling is so old-fashioned, it makes the bag look cheap. You have to really love the 1950s “retro” look, to like the overall appearance. The bag definitely looks handmade, but it also looks crudely rustic.

Second, although the bag has lots of zippered compartments (inside and outside), it is only 3” deep. It has no expansion gussets, so the total capacity is one laptop or one very thick sheaf of documents. Internal zipper compartments are relatively useless if a bag can’t expand to hold the things added to the compartments.

Third, the bag is difficult to open. It opens with two metal clasps--these are hidden beneath the purely decorative buckled front straps. You have to pull up on both clasps at once to lift the flap, and you can’t do this easily without laying the bag flat on one side, or holding it on your lap. The leather flap itself is very stiff (at least when the bag is new), and this adds to the opening difficulty.

Fourth, the bag has no locking mechanism. Not that it is easy to open (see previous paragraph).

Fifth, the brass fittings must tarnish very easily, because the bag arrives with every single exposed brass piece wrapped tightly in thin plastic wrap. It takes something very sharp to cut the plastic, and you must be careful not to scratch the fittings. (I succeeded in removing the wrappings without damaging the bag, but I punctured my left wrist with an Olfa knife in the process.)

The bag is reasonably priced (about $90 on Amazon). It comes with a snap-on shoulder carrying strap, and has a sturdy, permanently attached satchel handle. The handle is very comfortable. The bag leather is already distressed, so you needn’t worry about scratches. This is a truly rugged laptop bag.
text_fidelity_b: Leather Laptop Messenger Bag for Men - Handmade Laptop Briefcase Satchel by Leather Centric

Logitech Rechargeable Touchpad T650 with Windows 8 Multi-Touch Navigation - Black I am loving the Logitech Rechargeable Touchpad T650 with its user-friendly ease of use and many great features. The small size of 5 1/4" width x 5" length, smooth surface, rechargeable battery, very responsive with light-touch to activate gestures, on/off switch, place anywhere to use and sturdy design makes this the perfect touchpad for me. I got this touchpad as my computer mouse stopped working. I thought about a touchscreen monitor, but opted for this touchpad instead as it would be so nice to not have to stretch and fatigue my arm with the actions needed with a touchscreen monitor. The touchpad only needs a very light touch of the fingers to click, slide and navigate the gestures to activate the product features, which is most excellent to keep stress off the fingers. I have a desktop computer with Windows 7 right now, but this touchpad supports Windows 8 when I make the change which is another plus for me. Note a gesture not listed on the Logitech site that I just happen to notice worked to activate the right mouse click is a very light tap of two fingers in the middle of the touchpad. Also, note that a two-handed gesture not listed on the Logitech site that I found useful to highlight is to apply pressure to the left-hand bottom corner of the touchpad with the other hand lightly touch the touchpad with a smooth move of the cursor to highlight, then release the pressure on the touchpad to end highlighting-- after you have finished with copy and paste or drag and drop, to release the highlighted text--place the cursor on the highlighted area then lightly tap anywhere on the touchpad with one finger. Make sure to download the latest version of software for this touchpad to avoid possible glitches. It took me less than a day to get used to using this touchpad, and I find this touchpad superior to a mouse. I highly recommend this rechargeable touchpad and hope this review is helpful to others.

Tips for this touchpad's gestures (includes some that I wrote above):

(1.) To activate the right mouse click is a very light tap of two fingers in the middle of the touchpad.

(2.) A two-handed gesture to highlight is to apply pressure to the left-hand bottom corner of the touchpad and with the other hand lightly touch the touchpad with a smooth move of the cursor to highlight, then release the pressure on the touchpad to end highlighting-- after you have finished with copy and paste or drag and drop, to release the highlighted text--place the cursor on the highlighted area then lightly tap anywhere on the touchpad with one finger.

(3.) Download the latest version of software for this touchpad to avoid possible glitches.

(4.) Use the on/off switch on the top right side of touchpad to turn off when not in use for a long period of time to save the rechargeable battery.

Ring Video Doorbell 2 with HD Video, Motion Activated Alerts, Easy Installation called due to battery not charging although we spent the money to hard wire it..... and got an email from them. box says it works to -5F. this is what the email states..... Important temperatures

The following are key temperatures to watch out for in regards to your batteries.

36°F (3°C): The battery may not hold a charge as effectively, resulting in you having to charge the unit more frequently.
32°F (0°C): The battery may not charge at all. Even hardwired configurations may not charge the battery.
-5°F (-20.5°C): The battery may stop working completely until temperatures warm up.
What to do when it gets cold

Bring your device inside: When it gets cold and your device's battery runs out, bring your entire device inside and charge the battery with a USB cord. This will allow your device to warm up while the battery charges.
Make sure your battery is charged to 100%: When charging your battery, be sure that it reaches 100% before your remount the device. While the battery still won't be as effective as when the temperatures are warmer, making sure that the battery is at 100% will allow your device to work as long as possible.
Monitor your charge and the temperature: As long as the temperature hovers around the points listed above, you may have issues with battery charge. Therefore it's important to constantly monitor your battery life when it gets cold to make sure your device is always working.

NETGEAR WiFi Mesh Range Extender EX6400 - Coverage up to 2100 sq.ft. and 35 devices with AC1900 Dual Band Wireless Signal Booster & Repeater (up to 1900Mbps speed), plus Mesh Smart Roaming I have been using NETGEAR products for many years and am quite familiar with how they work and their quirks.

The fact that this unit has a built in Ethernet port is what led me to wanting this WiFi extender - the smart TV which is farthest from the primary router has had difficulty maintaining a solid connection so I wanted to utilize the Ethernet port on this extender to plug my TV directly into.

Set up of the extender was fairly straightforward, I plugged it into a power supply and ran an Ethernet cable from it to my laptop. The NETGEAR EXTENDER setup program auto loaded and was easy to follow. I setup the router to keep my same network name and password, it saved all of the information to my extender without issue. I unplugged the extender from both the power supply and my computer and located it into the bedroom, plugged it in and it found and connected to my WiFi without any issue. I plugged the smart TV into the Ethernet port and it connected beautifully - loading Netflix, HULU and Amazon Prime lightning fast.

The only hiccup happened when I finished that as the rest of my network went haywire with my smart devices not connecting and reconnecting. I restarted my modem and my primary router and everything appears to be back to operating as normal. I’m not sure what caused the glitch.

I can definitely see a WiFi speed increase in the area of the house that the extender is located and the TV that is plugged into the Ethernet port is streaming perfectly.

I am very pleased with this extender and would recommend it to anyone who needed to extend their WiFi range or provide an Ethernet Port to a device that is too far from their current hub.
text_fidelity_b: NETGEAR WiFi Mesh Range Extender EX6400 - Coverage up to 2100 sq.ft. and 35 devices with AC1900 Dual Band Wireless Signal Booster & Repeater (up to 1900Mbps speed), plus Mesh Smart Roaming

TP-Link N300 Wireless Portable Nano Travel Router(TL-WR802N) - WiFi Bridge/Range Extender/Access Point/Client Modes, Mobile in Pocket I purchased this to try and create my own wireless network within a hospital room I would be in for a while. The problem as many have stated is most commercial WiFi system require you log into a splash page after you connect to their network. This router does not have a way to do that. You can try using one of your devices and then clone the MAC address to the router, but this only works if this router is connected to the network with the Ethernet cable port. Most hotels and hospitals no longer have working Ethernet jacks in rooms. If you try and clone the MAC address on the wireless port it creates a conflict and everything stops working.

So to sum up, it works fine as a cheap travel router, but if you have to deal with a splash page on an WiFi only network, it simply will not work. It can’t be that hard to create one of these with a built in browser for splash pages. Anyone listening????

text_fidelity_a:
1MORE iBFree In-Ear Earphones Wireless Headphones with Bluetooth 4.2 AAC, IPX 6 Waterproof, Secure Fit, In-Line Mic for Sports Gym Running - New Model Black We blow through ear buds in our house and it seems that everyone has different ones that they like and don't like. Let's see how these measure up:

WHAT ARE THESE EAR BUDS LIKE?
These ear buds come in a nice box with a little instruction booklet. There is a little bag with three sets of gel caps in it. There are also three sets of hooks. Each of them comes in small medium and large. The hooks keep the buds in the ear but are soft so they don't hurt the ear at all.

The controls are on the right ear- the top hits about where the chin is. The connecting cord is big enough to be worn in front or back. The set comes with a cord but you have to have your own USB access to plug it into whether it be on an outlet or computer.

COMFORT
One of the most comfortable and secure earbud/headsets we have used to date- love that the hooks that help hold them in are soft so they don't hurt the ear, even after worn for a while.

PERFORMANCE
VOLUME
The headset gets the best result for us with the volume on max on the headset and halfway on the tablet that we use it with.

HIGHS/LOWS/MIDS
One of the things with this headset is that the highs are really nice and strong and so are the lows. The problem seems to be that the mids are drowned out making it feel like it is a bit out of balance. We have messed with it quite a bit and it seems to be the way it is.

SOUND PROOFING
These have excellent sound insulation capabilities. That does mean, however, that you need to be careful where you are wearing them if you need to hear what is around you or not.

BATTERY ALERT
When you first turn on the headphones, it will identify itself, tell you it is pairing and then give you an idea of how much battery life you have left- low, medium, or high.

POWER BUTTON
The power button is nice. Volume/skip functions are a challenge to get used to as compared to other Bluetooth headsets. There are sequences and timing as compared to others which seem to be simpler to use.

PAIRING
Very good pairing on all of the different devices we tested this with- several phones from Moto G3, Blu phone, Samsung Tablets and our stereo (forgot brand)

CHARGE
A charge has been lasting a good six to eight hours for us. Recharging seems to take us about three hours.

THE BOTTOM LINE
These are comfortable headphones that are easy to use, stay in the ears well, and have good insulation from ambient noise in the room or surroundings. They have nice highs and lows but tend to drown out the mids. The controls are a bit more challenging to learn at first as compared to other Bluetooth head sets we have used.

MY RATING
FOUR AND A HALF STARS- not able to give that so I am doing four. It is more like four and a half. The sound could be a little more balanced, and the controls not quite so difficult, but this is still a great set of headphones and we like it a lot.
text_fidelity_b: 1MORE iBFree In-Ear Earphones Wireless Headphones with Bluetooth 4.2 AAC, IPX 6 Waterproof, Secure Fit, In-Line Mic for Sports Gym Running - New Model Black

text_fidelity_a:
VideoSecu Low Profile TV Wall Mount Bracket for Most 32" - 75" LCD LED UHD Plasma HDTV, Compatible with Sony Bravia Samsung LG Haier Vizio Sharp AQUOS Westinghouse Pioneer ProScan Toshiba 1NN The bracket is incredible! I used it on a Samsung Plasma 60 inch ,(600x400-Vesa) PN60F5500. At first I was a little wary. The plasma is 2013 model ,weighs by itself about 60 pounds.Its solid, and the weight of my TV held it down without using security brackets. You need at least an 18 inch long screw driver because you cannot reach behind it once installed. A few turns and you're set. I found it easier to unscrew , first tighten , then go in the opposite direction so it locks the screwdriver in the center making it easier to remove. I left it untighten, since it held in place without them.

Im not a professional installer (like drilling holes and finding a stud in the wall) but was able to use my old screws from the wall to install this mount from my older plasma.. I did however have to drill 2 more at the bottom because of the Vesa difference. Beyond that, everything else was simple.Its solid once installed, very easy, and simple to understand.

CON: Personal pet peeve. The only con is on 60 inch TVs you cannot reach behind easily to use the security brackets.You have to use an 18 inch long screw driver or similar size to tighten them. (booklet does not say this . Only says use a screwdriver)They are not needed because the weight of the TV holds in in place. In my opinion, I like to do everything by the instructions. Not tighten the security brackets made me feel like I skipped a step. I will say its stays in place, and does not move, jiggle etc. Lifting the bottom of a 60 inch is not easy, so there is no worry about it being easily done, even by a kid since the hooks are on the top. Other reviewers have said security brackets are not needed to hold it in place. I just left them barely connected so I could have the option to screw on later.

PS: If you own a 60 inch and im guessing 65 (max size), it will not look like the picture after adding the back portions on the TV. At first I was under the impression it would not work, but adjusted the height on the TV brackets and it fit barely, but did fit.It does work on a (600x400) vesa mount TV.
text_fidelity_b: VideoSecu Low Profile TV Wall Mount Bracket for Most 32" - 75" LCD LED UHD Plasma HDTV, Compatible with Sony Bravia Samsung LG Haier Vizio Sharp AQUOS Westinghouse Pioneer ProScan Toshiba 1NN

text_fidelity_a:
Soundcore by Anker Life Q30 Hybrid Active Noise Cancelling Headphones with Multiple Modes, Hi-Res Sound, Custom EQ via App, 40H Playtime, Comfortable Fit, Bluetooth Headphones, Multipoint Connection These are very good travel headphones. Over-the-ear style is very comfortable when worn for hours at a time. The headphones are relatively lightweight and compact. They fold nicely into the included EVA soft-shell case, which fits easily into my carry-on bag.

The headphones pair easily with my Android smartphone. The Soundcore smartphone app is required for upgrading the headphones' firmware. The app also lets you customize the equalization to one of the presets or you can design your own. Depending on the kind of music you are listening to, the equalizer can make a noticeable difference in clarity and balance.

Unfortunately, the app spams me with notifications about unrelated Anker products. Hopefully this will not be frequent.

Noise cancellation works well. There are 3 modes: on, off (normal), and transparency that lets you talk to people around you without taking the headphones off. Noise cancellation can be toggled both from the app and from a button on the headphones themselves.

Overall, sound quality is good. More of a balanced sound than the boomy default effects that some headphones give. I mostly listen to acoustic music, so this works well for me. Clarity is good. Bluetooth connectivity has been great so far.
text_fidelity_b: Soundcore by Anker Life Q30 Hybrid Active Noise Cancelling Headphones with Multiple Modes, Hi-Res Sound, Custom EQ via App, 40H Playtime, Comfortable Fit, Bluetooth Headphones, Multipoint Connection

I have been insistent on an outdoor yagi style antenna for years. Having moved recently I found a decent yagi online and was prepared to pay about 3 times the cost of this antenna. Then the wife found this one and I decided to give it a shot because it was cheap. I figured I'd end up giving it to someone at work and buying the yagi antenna I had picked. I sat it on a table and connected it to my Amazon recast and reception was a bit choppy. Then I put the amplifier in line and plugged it in. I pulled in every channel available crystal clear. No stutter or tiling in the picture for any channel. Our stations broadcast anywhere between 20 to 40 miles away. I currently have the antenna sitting on a window sill until The weekend comes and I can run the cable and mount it in the attic. Works great at 40 miles or less. Would love a chance to try it out at 70 miles away just out of curiosity but I'm not about to move again to try it!

text_fidelity_a:
ANNKE C800 4K 8MP PoE Security Camera with Audio Recording, 4K Ultra HD IP Turret Camera, 100ft EXIR 2.0 Night Vision, H.265+, IP67 Weatherproof, Support 256GB SD Card(Not Included) When I initially saw this camera it checked most of the boxes I look for when looking for security cameras. It is PoE, has H.265, ONVIF support allowing use with Blue Iris, Sony IMX274 Starvis Sensor. Once I received this camera and began digging into it I quickly realized certain important facts.

Most importantly, this is a rebranded Hikvision camera. This is among the companies that has been discovered spying on the US using their cameras - the firmware this camera comes with is long outdated and, in fact, can not be updated to anywhere close to what is current. This is far too risky for me to install on my system.

Any camera you install on your system should have the latest firmware installed and you need to have a good understanding of network security protocols. Cameras such as this one, that are older versions of cameras made by manufacturers that are blacklisted - while still being sold, people who understand the industry avoid them - are an invitation for hackers to invade your system.

While the specs on and price of this camera seem decent - this is not a camera I recommend. This poses far more risks than it is worth.

text_fidelity_a:
Geeni Sentry Wi-Fi Wireless Smart Floodlight Security Camera, 2-Way Audio, Motion Sensor Alarm, Audio Video Recording, Works with Alexa and Hey Google I ordered the 'Geeni, Sentry Floodlight Security Camera with Motion Sensor, Intruder Alarm and Audio Video Recording' for review and would like to share my thoughts.

So I have had this camera for a while now and finally got it installed a couple of weeks ago and I am ready to share my thoughts and experience so far. This camera requires hard wiring which is why it took so long to get it installed. In my old home it was going to require me to get an extension cord, drill through my wall in the garage and plug it in, in the garage. This was much more work than I had anticipated. Now the new home already had normal motion sensor lights installed on switches, which made this more feasible for me to install. I took one of the motion sensor lights down and had to retrofit a new mount out of a piece of wood to cover the original hole left by removing the old light. This wasn't to hard to do and the Geeni light mounted with ease. Once installed and I turned the light switch on, it was ready to set up which took some time to do. I had to reset the device several times to get the App to set it up properly which was a quite pain however.

The camera itself is very good but so far I am not happy with all the notifications that I get which seem to be false alerts. It seems that everything seems to trigger this thing with absolutely no control as to how sensitive you would like the sensor to be. This is truly my main con with this device. I ended up turning notifications off on my mobile device which kind of defeats the purpose really.

Then there is the App which has thus far been pretty buggy. It has crashed many times and it is not so easy to find the "actual" activity that it seems to detect. Of all the motion activity that it detects, I would say that only 40% of it is relative. I do have the App set to just record everything (continuous) on the 128gb SD card which makes more sense seeing as there are so many false readings.

As for the good of this Geeni device, the image quality both during daytime and nighttime recording and playback is great. There is very little lag when accessing the footage which is surprising as I have other WiFi cameras that are painfully slow to connect and playback footage. This is probably my favorite feature (when the App doesn't crash).

Overall I do like this motion sensor and think that there is absolute value to it. I am however, really hoping for a firmware update which might help with some of the issues and allow you to adjust the sensitivity of the motion detection. Also it would be nice to have an easier way to track down and view "actual" activity rather than having to try and find that exact moment of capture. It seems to just tag a portion of footage, and you need to watch several minutes before you can find what it detected. You are also able to save the footage via the App, but doing so can take several days for it to show up on your mobile device which is another downside to this device.

I hope that this was helpful.
text_fidelity_b: Geeni Sentry Wi-Fi Wireless Smart Floodlight Security Camera, 2-Way Audio, Motion Sensor Alarm, Audio Video Recording, Works with Alexa and Hey Google

Fitbit Versa Smart Watch, Peach/Rose Gold Aluminium, One Size (S & L Bands Included), Heart Rate Monitor I got the FitBit Versa because I wanted to try a smart watch without having to buy an expensive Apple Watch. The FitBit is comfortable to wear and looks nice. I like that it tracks my heart rate and steps. What I really wanted was to see my notifications on my watch. This watch allows you to see your notifications and will even vibrate to remind you of events on your phone calendar. It is lacking in a couple areas. One— you can see your notifications but you cannot interact with them at all. It also only shows text, so if someone texts you a gif or emoji it shows up as a blank message. It also doesn’t consistently give me my notifications, but that could be a phone setting issue. Second— the available apps are limited. You can play music, but only from a couple platforms. You cannot play Amazon music, audible, Scribd, podcaster... Also, the fertility tracking app for FitBit is ridiculously limiting. It is possibly the worst tracking I have ever seen. Since that is in the realm of health, I think it should be a lot better. It is effectively unusable.
So while this is a cheaper option than others and has heart rate tracking and such, there are still some limitations. It is waterproof— so I can wear it in the pool. Battery lasts about 3 days on one charge. And you can customize the watch face to your liking.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Versa Smart Watch, Peach/Rose Gold Aluminium, One Size (S & L Bands Included), Heart Rate Monitor
